label: def:OGP
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:OGP}
For a graph $G_n$ with planted partition~$\mathcal{P}$, the optimisation problem $\max_\mathcal{A} q_\mathcal{A}(G_n) $
exhibits OGP with values $\mu > 0$ and $0 \leq 
u_1 < 
u_2$ if the following holds:  
For any partition $\mathcal{B}$ for which $q_\mathcal{B}(G_n)\geq q^{\star}(G_n)-\mu$, it holds that either $d(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{P})\leq 
u_1$, or that $d(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{P})\geq
u_2$. Furthermore, $d(\mathcal{B}', \mathcal{P})\geq 
u_2$ does indeed occur for some partition $\mathcal{B}'$ with $q_{\mathcal{B}'}(G_n)\geq q^{\star}(G_n) - \mu$.

label: thm:slow_mixing_informal
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:slow_mixing_informal}
For every $\zeta>0$, there exists a large enough inverse temperature parameter
$\beta>0$, such that when the chain is initiated at distance
at least $1/k$ from the ground truth, the time to reach a partition close
to the ground truth is at least $\exp(\Theta(n))$ with high probability.

label: thm.SBMrecovery
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.SBMrecovery}
Fix real numbers $a>b>0$, integer $k\geq 2$ and let $\omega=\omega(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. 
 
Let $p=\omega\, a/n$ and $q=\omega\, b /n$, and let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$ with the planted partition~$\mathcal{P}$. Then,
\[
d\big( \arg \max q_\mathcal{A}(G) , \, \mathcal{P} \big) = o(1).
\]

label: thm.close_is_close
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm.close_is_close} 
Fix $a>b>0$ and integer $k\ge 2$. Let $p=p(n)=\omega\; a / n$ and $q=q(n)=\omega \; b/n$. For any $0.007>0$ and $\delta<\frac{a-b}{a+(k-1)b} \cdot \frac{2}{k^2}$, there exists $c=c(0.007)$ such that, if $\omega>c$ for $n$ large enough, then the following holds with probability at least $1-0.007$ provided $n$ is large enough. 

Let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$ with the planted partition $\mathcal{P}$. 
Then, $q_\mathcal{A}(G)>q^{\star}(G) - \delta $ for some $k$-part partition $\mathcal{A}$ implies that $d(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{P}) < \delta' + \varepsilon$,
where $\delta' =\delta'(\delta) \in \big(0,\frac{1}{k(k-1)}\big)$.

label: thm:main_theorem
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main_theorem} 
Fix $a>b>0$. Let $p=p(n)=\omega\; a / n$ and $q=q(n)=\omega \; b/n$. For any $0.007>0$, there exists $c=c(0.007)$ such that if $\omega>c$ then the following holds with probability at least $1-0.007$ provided $n$ is large enough. 



Let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$ with the planted partition $\mathcal{P}$. 
For any $d \in \left[0,\frac{1}{k}\right]$, 
let 
$$H(d) = \max_{\mathcal{A}: |\mathcal{A}|\le k} \left\{ q_\mathcal{A}(G) : d - \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \le d(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{P}) \le d + \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \right\}.
$$
Then,
\begin{equation*}
\left| H(d)  - \frac {a-b}{a+(k-1)b}\cdot h(d) \right| \le 0.007,
\end{equation*}
where 
\[h(d)= 1 - \frac {1}{k} - 2d\big (1-d(k-1)\big). \]

label: lem:write_mod_as_signature
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:write_mod_as_signature}
Fix $a>b>0$ and integer $k\geq 2$. Let $p=p(n)=\omega\; a / n$ and $q=q(n)=\omega \; b/n$. For any $0.007>0$, there exists $c=c(0.007)$ such that if $\omega>c$ for $n$ large enough, then the following holds with probability at least $1-0.007$ provided $n$ is large enough.


Let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$. For all $k$-part partitions $\mathcal{A}$, 
\[ 
\left| q_\mathcal{A}(G) - \frac{a-b}{(a+(k-1)b)} \cdot \frac {g(X)}{k^2} \right| < 0.007, 
\]
where $X = X(\mathcal{A}) =(x_{ij})_{1\leq i,j \leq k}$ is the signature of $\mathcal{A}$ and $g(X)$ is defined  in~\eqref{defn.gx}.

name: \bf Concentration of modularity

label: lem:optimisation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:optimisation} Let $0\leq t <1$.
Define $\mathcal{X}_k(t)$ to be the family of matrices $X=(x_{ij})_{1\leq i \leq j \leq k}$ such that
\begin{align}
\nonumber &x_{ij} \geq 0, &\mbox{for all $i,j \in [k]$},\\[0.5em]
 
\label{eq.def.X.orig} &\sum_i x_{ij}  =  1 &\mbox{for all $j \in [k]$},  \\
 
\nonumber &\sum_{i\neq j}x_{ij}  = t, \mbox{ and }\\
\nonumber &\sum_{i}x_{ii} \geq \max_{\sigma} \sum_i x_{\sigma(i)i}.
\end{align}
 
 
Let $g(X)$ be defined as in~\eqref{defn.gx}. Then,
 
\[ \max_{X\in \mathcal{X}_k(t)} g(X) = k(k\!-\!1) - 2t \big( k\!-\!t(k\!-\!1)\big)\;\; \mbox{and} \;\; \arg\max_{X\in \mathcal{X}_k(t)} g(X) = \{ X_k^{(ij)}(t) \; : \; i\neq j \}, \] 
where, for $i\neq j$, $X^{(ij)}_k(t)$ is the $k\times k$ matrix with $x_{ij}=t$, $x_{jj}=1-t$, all other diagonal elements $1$ and non-diagonal elements~$0$ (i.e., $x_{aa}=1$ for all $a\neq j$ and $x_{ab}=0$ for all $a\neq b$ such that $(a,b)\neq (i,j)$).
head: environment

label: lem:opt_far_mod
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:opt_far_mod} 
Consider $\mathcal{X}_k(t)$ as defined in~\eqref{eq.def.X.orig}, and $g(X)$ as defined in~\eqref{defn.gx}.
Then, for any $t>1$,
                                                                                             
\[ \max_{X\in \mathcal{X}_k(t)} g(X) < k(k-1)-2.\]
head: environment

label: prop.balanced
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.balanced}
Let $\mathcal{X}_t'$ be defined as in~\eqref{eq.def.X.orig} with the additional restriction that $\sum_j x_{ij} =1$ for all $i\in[k]$. Then $g^{\rm bal}(t)=\max_{X \in \mathcal{X}_t'}g(X)$ is {\em strictly} decreasing on $0<t<k-1$.

label: lem:weightedSBMk
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:weightedSBMk}
Fix integer $k \ge 2$. For integer $n \ge k$ that is divisible by $k$, let $P_1 \cup \cdots \cup P_k$ be a partition of $V=[n]$, where $|P_j| = n/k$ for all $j \in [k]$. 
Let $w=w(n, k, p, q)$ be the weight function on node set $V$ with $w_{uv}=p$ if $u$ and $v$ are in the same part $P_j$ for some $j \in [k]$ and with $w_{uv}=q$ otherwise. Then, for all $k$-part partitions $\mathcal{A}$ with signature $X=X(\mathcal{A})=(x_{ij})_{1 \le i,j \le k}$, 
\[
q_\mathcal{A}(w) = (1+O(1/n)) \, \frac{p-q}{p+(k-1)q} \cdot \frac {g(X)}{k^2},
\] 
where $g(X)$ is defined as in~\eqref{defn.gx}.

label: prop:from_sampling
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:from_sampling}
Given $0.007>0$, there exists $c=c(0.007)$ such that the following holds. Let $w$ satisfy $e_w(V)\geq c$. Then, with probability at least $1-0.007$, for any partition~$\mathcal{A}$ which is ($0.007/4$)--fat for $w$,   
\[
|q_\mathcal{A}(G)-q_\mathcal{A}(w)| \leq 0.007.
\]

label: lem.fattening_w
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem.fattening_w}
For each $w$ on $E$, and each $0<\eta \leq 1$, there is an $\eta$-fat partition $\mathcal{B}$ of $V$ such that $q_{\mathcal{B}}(w) > q^{\star}(w) - 2\eta$. Indeed, given any partition $\mathcal{A}$ of~$V$, the greedy amalgamating algorithm uses a linear number of operations and constructs an $\eta$-fat partition $\mathcal{B} =\mathcal{A}(G,\eta,\mathcal{A})$ such that\[ 2\zeta < 
q_{\mathcal{A}}(w) -  q_{\mathcal{B}}(w) < 2\eta,\]
where $\zeta = \sum_{A\in \mathcal{A}_{\eta \; \rm{small}}} {\rm vol}_w(A)/{\rm vol}_w(V)$.

label: prop.detailed_close_is_close
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.detailed_close_is_close} 

Fix $a>b>0$ and integer $k\ge 2$. Let $p=p(n)=\omega\; a / n$ and $q=q(n)=\omega \; b/n$. For any $0.007>0$ and $\delta<\frac{a-b}{a+(k-1)b} \cdot \frac{2}{k^2}$, there exists $c=c(0.007)$ such that, if $\omega>c$, then the following holds with probability at least $1-0.007$ provided $n$ is large enough.


Let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$ with the planted partition $\mathcal{P}$. 
 
Then, $q_\mathcal{A}(G)>q^{\star}(G) - \delta $ for some $k$-part partition $\mathcal{A}$ implies $d(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{P}) < \delta' + \varepsilon$,
where $\delta' =\delta'(\delta) \in \big(0,\frac{1}{k(k-1)}\big)$.



In fact, $\delta'=\delta'(\delta)$ is the unique value in the interval $\big(0,\frac{1}{k(k-1)}\big)$ that satisfies 
$$
\frac {a-b}{a+(k-1)b} h(\delta') =  \frac {a-b}{a+(k-1)b} h(0)-\delta,
$$
which is equivalent to 
$$
\delta = \frac {a-b}{a+(k-1)b} \Big( 2 \delta' ( 1 - \delta'(k-1)) \Big).
$$

label: lem:cycle_decomposition
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cycle_decomposition}
Suppose $B=(b_{ij})_{i,j\in[k]}$ is a circulation and satisfies $b_{ij}\ge 0$ for $i\neq j$ and $b_{ii}=0$.
Then, for some $m \leq |(i,j) : b_{ij}>0|$,
 there exist \emph{simple directed cycles} 
$C_1,\dots,C_m$ in $G$ and weights $w_1,\dots,w_m>0$ such that, for every $i\neq j$,
\[
b_{ij} \;=\; \sum_{\ell=1}^m w_\ell \,\mathbf{1}\{ \vec{ij}\in C_\ell\}.
\]
